The Prophet ﷺ said: If you are faithful to your duty, even if you do not see the fruits, you will be among the successful. Ilyas did not see the fruits of his labour. But his name is recited in the Quran. And every Muslim who reads Surah As-Saffat today sends salam upon him.

dialogue.arabic: سَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ إِلْ يَاسِينَ
dialogue.translation: Peace be upon Ilyasin.

lessons.didYouKnow: The name Ilyasin in this verse is sometimes interpreted as a variant of Ilyas, and sometimes as a reference to the family of Ilyas. Either way, Allah honours Ilyas — and his followers — with the same peace given to the greatest prophets.
lessons.takeaway: Allah does not measure you by your results — He measures you by your faithfulness.

lessons.title: The Teaching of the Few
lessons.body:
One of the great lessons of Ilyas's mission is the value of the few. His entire nation rejected him — except a handful. And Allah still honoured him with a place among the elect. Not because of the many who believed — but because of his own faithfulness.

This is a reminder for every believer who feels outnumbered. There are times in every generation when truth is unpopular. When the majority has abandoned the way of Allah. When the faithful are a tiny remnant among the mocking crowd. And in those moments, the believer might feel that their smallness means their failure.

But the Quran teaches the opposite. Nuh called for 950 years, and only a few believed. Ilyas called for years, and a handful followed him. The Prophet ﷺ himself, in the early years of Islam, was followed by a small group of the weak and the poor. And yet — all of them were honoured by Allah with names that are spoken until the end of time.

The Prophet ﷺ said: Islam began as something strange, and it will return to being something strange, so glad tidings to the strangers. The Muslims who remain faithful when the world has turned away are the true inheritors of the prophetic mission. They are the new Ilyases — standing firm in a world of Ba'ls.

dialogue.arabic: بَدَأَ الْإِسْلَامُ غَرِيبًا، وَسَيَعُودُ غَرِيبًا، فَطُوبَىٰ لِلْغُرَبَاءِ
dialogue.translation: Islam began as something strange, and it will return to being something strange, so glad tidings to the strangers.

lessons.didYouKnow: The classical scholars describe Ilyas as one of the four prophets who never died — the others being Idris, Isa, and al-Khidr (according to some narrations). Some say Ilyas will return at the end of time alongside Isa to renew the faith of the believers.
lessons.takeaway: Being few is not being forgotten — Allah remembers those the world ignores.

lessons.title: The Legacy of Ilyas
lessons.body:
Ilyas is one of the least-discussed prophets in the Quran — only a few verses, only one full passage. And yet, the honour given to him is extraordinary. He is called of the messengers. He is honoured with the same peace that Allah sends upon Ibrahim. He is praised for calling his people away from the false god Ba'l and back to the Lord of their forefathers.

His legacy is a simple one: confront the false gods, call to the One God, and be faithful even when no one listens. This is the eternal mission of the prophets. And Ilyas carried it with patience, with courage, and with a heart that never wavered.

The Prophet ﷺ said: Every prophet has a mission, and mine is the mission of mercy. But the missions of the prophets before him — Ilyas among them — were missions of warning, of confrontation, of standing alone against a nation that had abandoned its Lord.

Ilyas's example is for every believer who lives in a time and place where truth is unpopular. It is a reminder that the call to tawhid does not require applause. It does not require success. It does not require the acceptance of the majority. It only requires faithfulness. And Ilyas was faithful.

May Allah make us among the faithful — even when the world has turned away. Ameen.

dialogue.arabic: سَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ إِلْ يَاسِينَ ۝ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ
dialogue.translation: Peace be upon Ilyasin. Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good.

lessons.didYouKnow: Ilyas is honoured in the Quran with the same blessing formula used for Ibrahim and Nuh. It is one of the highest honours given to any prophet — and it is given to a man whose story is barely told.
lessons.takeaway: The greatest honour is not a long story — it is a faithful life.

lessons.title: The Successor of Ilyas
lessons.body:
Al-Yasa (AS) — known in the Bible as Elisha — is one of the least-mentioned prophets of the Quran. Only two verses name him, and neither verse tells us a single detail about his life. He is simply mentioned as one of the prophets whom Allah favoured above the worlds.

The Quran says: And We gave him Ishaq and Yaqub — each We guided. And Nuh, We had guided before. And from his descendants, Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub, Yusuf, Musa, and Harun. Thus do We reward the doers of good. And Zakariyya, Yahya, Isa, and Ilyas — each was of the righteous. And then, in the same list: And Ismail, Al-Yasa, Yunus, and Lut — and all We preferred over the worlds.

Read that list. Al-Yasa is placed alongside Ismail, Yunus, and Lut — three of the great prophets of revelation. In a single verse, Allah gathers him among the elect. No story. No details. No conversation. Just the honour.

And yet, the classical narrations say Al-Yasa was the successor of Ilyas — the prophet who continued his mission after Ilyas passed. He did not begin a new message — he carried the old one forward. He did not plant a new seed — he watered the seed that his predecessor had already planted.

dialogue.arabic: وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَالْيَسَعَ وَيُونُسَ وَلُوطًا ۚ وَكُلًّا فَضَّلْنَا عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ
dialogue.translation: And Ismail, Al-Yasa, Yunus, and Lut — and all We preferred over the worlds.

lessons.didYouKnow: Al-Yasa is mentioned twice in the Quran — in Al-An'am 6:86 and Sad 38:48. Both times, he is honoured alongside other great prophets, and neither mention includes any narrative detail. The Quran deliberately preserves his rank, not his story.
lessons.takeaway: Allah does not always preserve the details of a prophet — He preserves the honour.

lessons.title: The Prophet of Continuity
lessons.body:
Al-Yasa's role was not to be a great innovator. He was not the first prophet of his line. He was not the one who brought a new book or a new law. He was the one who carried on. He came after Ilyas. He continued the mission. He kept the flame lit.

This is one of the great unnoticed callings in the history of prophethood. We remember the founders — Musa, Ibrahim, Nuh. But we forget the successors — those who came after and carried the message forward. Without the successors, the founders' work would die with them. Without those who continue, the mission ends.

The Quran calls Al-Yasa one of the muṣṭafīn — the chosen. And it adds: and all We preferred over the worlds. The Arabic phrase faḍḍalnā means 'We preferred, We favoured.' Al-Yasa was favoured by Allah — not because he did something extraordinary, but because he did the ordinary faithfully.

The Prophet ﷺ said: The deeds most beloved to Allah are those done consistently, even if they are small. Al-Yasa's consistency was his greatness. He was not the flash. He was the steady flame.

dialogue.arabic: وَكُلًّا فَضَّلْنَا عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ
dialogue.translation: And all We preferred over the worlds.

lessons.didYouKnow: The classical scholars say Al-Yasa lived among the Children of Israel after Ilyas, guiding them back to tawhid and calling them away from the worship of Ba'l. His mission was quieter than Ilyas's — but no less significant.
lessons.takeaway: The ones who carry the mission forward are as honoured as the ones who began it.

lessons.title: Among the Elect
lessons.body:
The Quran uses two phrases to describe Al-Yasa. First, in Surah Al-An'am, he is listed among those whom Allah preferred over the worlds — the same phrase used for Nuh, Ibrahim, and the other great prophets. Second, in Surah Sad, he is described as min al-akhyār — 'of the best.'

The Quran says: And remember Ismail, Al-Yasa, and Dhul-Kifl — all are of the best. Min al-akhyār. Not 'of the good' — of the best. The choicest of the chosen. The highest category that a human being can reach.

Al-Yasa received this title without a single story attached to his name. No battle. No miracle. No confrontation with a tyrant. And yet, the title of best is his. The Quran does not need to tell us what he did — because whatever he did, it was enough for Allah to call him one of the best.

This should comfort every believer who feels that their quiet faithfulness goes unnoticed. Allah sees the deeds that no one else sees. He knows the hours of prayer that no one else knows about. He remembers the patience that no one else witnessed. And one day, the quietest servant may be raised to the same rank as the loudest — because the standard of Allah is not what people saw, but what Allah knew.

dialogue.arabic: وَاذْكُرْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَالْيَسَعَ وَذَا الْكِفْلِ ۖ وَكُلٌّ مِّنَ الْأَخْيَارِ
dialogue.translation: And remember Ismail, Al-Yasa, and Dhul-Kifl — all are of the best.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Arabic word akhyār — the best — is the plural of khayr (good). It is a superlative: not just good, but the choicest of the good. Al-Yasa is honoured with this word without any narrative justification — because Allah's knowledge of him is enough.
lessons.takeaway: Allah knows your deeds even when no one else does — and His testimony is enough.

lessons.title: The Watered Seed
lessons.body:
There is a lesson in Al-Yasa's quietness that deserves its own reflection. When Ilyas called his people, they refused him. When Ilyas left, the seed of faith had been planted but not yet grown. And Al-Yasa came — not to plant again, but to water. Not to call from scratch, but to nurture what his predecessor had started.

And the seed grew. The narrations say that under Al-Yasa's guidance, the people of his land began to return to tawhid. Slowly, quietly, the way of Ilyas took root. Some of the people who had mocked Ilyas in his lifetime accepted the message in Al-Yasa's. The harvest belonged to both of them.

This is how the work of Allah unfolds in history. The one who plants is not always the one who harvests. Musa planted, and Yushu (Joshua) harvested. Ilyas planted, and Al-Yasa harvested. The Prophet ﷺ planted, and the Companions harvested. In every generation, there are those who sow and those who reap — and both are honoured by Allah.

The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever guides someone to good will have a reward like the one who did it, without diminishing the reward of the one who did it. Al-Yasa guided. And Ilyas — who had already passed — was still earning reward, because his seed had grown.

dialogue.arabic: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَىٰ خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ
dialogue.translation: Whoever guides someone to good will have a reward like the one who did it.

lessons.didYouKnow: The classical scholars identify Al-Yasa as the prophet who consolidated the Israelite return to tawhid after Ilyas. His quiet ministry produced a harvest that his predecessor could not see in his lifetime — and both were rewarded for it.
lessons.takeaway: The one who waters is as rewarded as the one who plants.

lessons.title: The Unknown Prophet
lessons.body:
Al-Yasa is called by some scholars al-nabī al-majhūl — 'the unknown prophet.' His story is barely known. His mission is barely described. His miracles are barely mentioned. And yet, the Quran places him among the elect. He is honoured in every prayer that Muslims recite when they send salam upon the prophets — because the Prophets are all mentioned in the tashahhud's blessing. Al-Yasa is included in that blessing by inclusion among the āli Ibrāhīm — the family of Ibrahim.

Think about the mercy of Allah in this. He did not require Al-Yasa to be famous. He did not require him to be remembered. He did not require his story to be preserved in detail. He simply required him to be faithful — and then He honoured him forever.

This is a reminder for every believer who feels invisible. The world may never know your name. The world may never record your deeds. The world may never honour your sacrifice. But Allah sees. Allah remembers. Allah records. And on the Day of Judgement, the ones the world forgot will stand beside the ones the world honoured — because Allah's measure is not the world's measure.

The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever is sincere in his faith, even if his deeds are few, will enter Paradise. Al-Yasa was sincere. And he entered. Not because of the many who remembered him, but because of the One who never forgot him.

dialogue.arabic: وَكُلٌّ مِّنَ الْأَخْيَارِ
dialogue.translation: And all are of the best.

lessons.didYouKnow: Some scholars suggest that Al-Yasa was the prophet who performed the miracle of purifying the water of Jericho and who received the mantle of Ilyas. The Quran does not confirm these details — but the traditions preserve his memory among the faithful.
lessons.takeaway: The world may forget you — but Allah never does.

lessons.title: The Legacy of Al-Yasa
lessons.body:
Al-Yasa's legacy is one of the most important in the Quran — and it is almost entirely unwritten. He is remembered as the prophet of continuation. He is honoured as one of the akhyār — the best. He is placed among the elect of Allah without a single narrative detail. And his example teaches us that the most important work in the history of faith is often the quietest.

Every generation of believers stands on the shoulders of those who came before them. The scholars who preserved the knowledge, the teachers who passed on the tradition, the parents who raised the next generation on tawhid — none of them may be famous. None of them may be remembered. But the work they did was essential to the survival of the faith.

Al-Yasa was that kind of person. He did not begin the mission — he continued it. He did not plant the seed — he watered it. He did not build the ark — he kept it afloat. And yet, the Quran honours him with the same titles given to the greatest prophets.

May Allah make us among the faithful servants — and honour us as He honoured Al-Yasa. Ameen.

dialogue.arabic: وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَالْيَسَعَ وَيُونُسَ وَلُوطًا ۚ وَكُلًّا فَضَّلْنَا عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ
dialogue.translation: And Ismail, Al-Yasa, Yunus, and Lut — and all We preferred over the worlds.

lessons.didYouKnow: Al-Yasa is the only prophet in the Quran whose mention is entirely without narrative — he is given nothing but titles of honour. His example teaches us that Allah's testimony about a person is worth more than any story the world could write about them.
lessons.takeaway: The greatest honour is not the story of your life — it is the witness of your Lord.
